issues.legal_issue: A fresh declaration cannot be made after the statutory time limit has expired, even when an earlier timely declaration has been quashed and a court has directed renewed acquisition proceedings.
material_facts: The land was covered by a notification published under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, on 8 September 1982.
A declaration under Section 6 was made within three years, but it was later quashed because of non-compliance with the applicable mandatory procedure.
The three-year period had expired before the High Court directed a fresh enquiry and allowed a further declaration to be issued.
The High Court also directed that an award be passed after any fresh declaration.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not authorize a fresh declaration after the three-year period had expired. Its directions for a fresh Section 5A enquiry, a further declaration, and a subsequent award were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, barred a declaration concerning land covered by the relevant Section 4(1) notification after three years from publication. Explanation 1 excluded from the computation only a period during which action or proceedings pursuant to that notification were stayed by a court. The judgment cites no earlier cases.

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning proceedings to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.earlier_declaration_quashed: A declaration concerning the land was made but was later set aside.
predicates.declaration_window_expired_before_fresh_: The applicable time window for making a declaration had expired before a fresh declaration could be made.

issues.definition: When an acquisition appeal concerns a quashed declaration and the applicable declaration window expired before a fresh declaration, a fresh declaration is not permitted.

issues.legal_issue: A stay ordered by an executive authority does not qualify for exclusion when computing the time limit for a land-acquisition declaration.
material_facts: In calculating the time limit, the acquiring authority relied on a stay granted by a government minister on a petition concerning an adjoining landowner's property.
The stay was not made by a court.
issues.conclusion: The minister's stay could not be taken into account when computing the period for making a declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Explanation 1 to the proviso to Section 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, excludes a period of stay only when the stay is ordered by a court. The judgment cites no earlier cases.

predicates.land_acquisition_time_limit_computation: The time available for making a declaration concerning land acquisition is being computed.
predicates.stay_order_made_by_nonjudicial_authority: An authority other than a court ordered a stay of acquisition-related action or proceedings.

issues.definition: When a nonjudicial authority orders a stay during computation of the time limit for an acquisition declaration, that stay is not excluded from the computation.

issues.legal_issue: A court stay concerning an adjoining owner's land does not suspend the time limit applicable to a different parcel covered by the same notification.
material_facts: An adjoining landowner obtained a court stay in proceedings concerning that owner's land.
The acquiring authority sought to rely on that stay when calculating the time limit for a declaration concerning the appellant's separate land.
The adjoining-land stay was granted after the applicable three-year period had expired.
issues.conclusion: The stay concerning the adjoining land could not be used to extend the time for making a declaration concerning the appellant's land.
issues.legal_principle: Explanation 1 to the proviso to Section 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, concerns a stay of action or proceedings relating to the land for which the declaration is required; a stay concerning an adjacent parcel cannot be used for another parcel. The judgment cites no earlier cases.

predicates.land_acquisition_time_limit_computation: The time available for making a declaration concerning a particular parcel is being computed.
predicates.court_stay_concerns_adjacent_parcel: A court stayed acquisition-related action or proceedings concerning a parcel adjoining, but distinct from, the parcel at issue.

issues.definition: When the time limit for a declaration concerning a parcel is computed, a court stay concerning a distinct adjoining parcel is not applied to that computation.
